Streamr iOS — what changed this pass

Recreated from the actual SwiftUI you now have (real colors, real generated icons, real copy) so you can flag what to change before this goes in front of Xcode. Brand audit

Checked colors, font, and logo assets in the app against the official Style Guide — not just assumed everything already matched.

On brand
  • Primary green #9AD0AF, warning gold #FFC978, and the purple→blue gradient #7A44B6 → #4768DA all match the official guide exactly — these were already correct.
  • Wordmark usage (login screen, in-app) is the right logo, just swapped to the newer official export — see "Fixed" for details.
  • Third-party platform icons (YouTube, Facebook, etc.) are intentionally left as-is — those are trademarked marks, not Streamr's to restyle.
Fixed this pass
  • App icon — was a hand-crop from the wordmark (had a stray "t"-crossbar bleeding in). Replaced with the official pre-made S logo square.png, downscaled and flattened for the App Store.
  • In-app wordmark — swapped to the official folder's re-export of the logo (visually identical to what was there, different file, now traceable to the sanctioned source).
  • Font code comment — fixed a stale TODO that said "Montserrat"; the official guide says Heebo. No font files bundled yet either way — still renders in system font.
Needs your call
  • Heebo vs. Montserrat — the live website's own CSS uses Montserrat, not Heebo. Either the site is off-brand/mid-rebrand, or Heebo is meant for marketing only. Worth a direct answer before bundling font files.
  • #D37778 (coral) is a core palette color in the guide but isn't used as a standalone accent anywhere in the app yet — only buried in a 5-color decorative gradient. What's it meant to represent?
  • The tagline art ("Your content. Your story. Yourself!") uses a third, bubbly display font — different from both Heebo and Montserrat. Marketing-only, or does it belong in-product somewhere?

App icon

Built from the official "S logo square" artwork (2000×2000, pre-made), downscaled to 1024 and flattened to opaque — required for the App Store. Replaces an earlier hand-cropped version.

Main Stream + navigation

Bottom tab bar replaces the old 3-tab layout. The center "Add Stream" button doesn't open a screen — it snaps back and presents the show-creation sheet. Hamburger (top right) is new.

Login — Google, Facebook, Apple

Wired against the real /onboarding/socialLogin contract. Apple uses the system-required button style; needs real credentials before any of the three work on a device.

Account → Settings → Destinations

New Settings screen (gear icon on Account) houses Destinations plus the legal links. Connect/disconnect works today; the auto-completing redirect flow needs a backend confirmation first (see README).

Built from the actual code in anchialine-ascent as of this session — colors/fonts/copy are pulled from Theme.swift, Typography.swift, and each view's real strings, not guessed. iOS system chrome (status bar, corner radii) is approximated for readability, not pixel-matched.
